candidates.statement: The following statements hold for standard probability- preserving systems. 4 1. There is a maximal measure-distal factor WY . It contains the invariant factor, and Y → WY is relatively weakly mixing. A distal factor pulls back into the maximal distal factor of any extension. Every measure-preserving automorphism commuting with R preserves WY . 2. Factors and joinings of distal systems are distal. A distal system is relatively distal over each of its factors. For every nonzero integer q, R is distal if and only if Rq is distal. 3. Relative weak mixing passes to nonzero integer powers and to conditionally independent base change. More generally, the product of relatively weakly mixing fibre laws over any invariant joining of their base laws is relatively weakly mixing over that joining. 4. A relatively weakly mixing extension and a relatively distal extension of the same base are relatively disjoint: the only invariant joining which identifies their base coordinates is the relatively independent joining. 5. If R is distal, then, for every d ≥ 1 and bounded g1, . . . , gd, the averages 1 N N X n=1 d Y i=1 gi(Rin y) converge almost surely. If (St Y )t∈R is a probability-preserving flow, the maximal distal factor WY of S1 Y is a flow factor. Its action at every nonzero rational time is distal.
candidates.cited_by: The existence assertion and the relatively weakly mixing extension are the Furstenberg– Zimmer structure theorem [9, 26]; its nonergodic probability-algebra formulation is given in [13, Theorems 1.1 and 1.2]. We recall the consequences needed here, with particular attention to changes of base and of time.
references: [9] H. Furstenberg, Ergodic behavior of diagonal measures and a theorem of Szemerédi on arithmetic progressions, J. Analyse Math. 31 (1977), 204–256.
[26] R. J. Zimmer, Extensions of ergodic group actions, Illinois J. Math. 20 (1976), no. 3, 373–409. doi:10.1215/ijm/1256049780.
[13] A. Jamneshan, An uncountable Furstenberg–Zimmer structure theory, Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems 43 (2023), no. 7, 2404–2436. doi:10.1017/etds.2022.43. Corrected version: arXiv:2103.17167v4.

manuscripts.title: A translational tile with no fully periodic tiling in dimension three

candidates.statement: For every finite nonempty graph G of order m, h(G) ≤ m + 4 cm(G) + 2 3 . In particular, if α(G) ≤ 2 and cm(G) < m/100, then h(G) < 26m 75 + 2 3 < m 2 ≤ χ(G) (m ≥ 5).

candidates.label: Theorem 6.3
candidates.name: Gradient realization
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.3 (Gradient realization).
candidates.statement: Suppose two units in fixed leaves have lists satisfying (6.2), the binary prescriptions yielding (6.3), equal matched keys, and an admissible injecting small table. Freeze their actual cross Gram entries whenever either argument is a pin or a key direction. Then there are abstract cross bilinear forms on the full nominal spaces, extending all these frozen entries, whose primal-versus-channel entries satisfy uzUi = r(viz) on X (i and z in opposite units). (6.4) Only the primal-versus-channel entries need be prescribed in the final test. Their number is at most 16|E|h dim B = O(n), with its coefficient fixed before M0. Agreement of the actual cross Grams with these entries produces all four cross holes, with witnesses (viz, vzi).

candidates.label: Proposition 7.1
candidates.name: Collision criterion
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.1 (Collision criterion).
candidates.statement: Let σ be a unit law in Theorem 3.1, and let e σ be a restriction of it of relative mass at least 2−o(N), decomposed into leaves satisfying (4.7). Mix the leaves with their actual masses in e σ. Suppose accepted numerical queries as above, with their leaf-pair choices of table and separate filters, satisfy Eindependent leaf pair Z dAdB dνn ≥ 2−o(N) . (7.3) Then two independent units from the original σ have all four cross holes with probability at least 2−(kmax+.03)N−o(N) . (7.4) 37 It suffices to obtain (7.3) after skipping some leaf pairs, or after summing over a bounded number of numerical options. Positive subsequential constants and inverse-polynomial overlap bounds both suffice. In particular, this conclusion contradicts a sequence violating Theorem 3.1.

candidates.label: Theorem 8.2
candidates.name: Phase alternative
candidates.heading: Theorem 8.2 (Phase alternative).
candidates.statement: Suppose a marked-unit law is obtained by restricting an admissible law in Theorem 3.1 to mass at least 10−12, and ∆O ̸= 0 throughout. For all sufficiently large n, one can retain a sublaw of fixed positive relative mass, bounded below using only the early parameters, such that one of the following holds for independent draws A, B: (i) every nontrivial phase mean E(−1)uB,S(∆A)+uA,R(∆B) , (S, R) ̸= (∅, ∅), has absolute value less than .005; (ii) a componentwise cover of total dimension at most d0 covers every ∆O, and every displayed mean for which |S| = 1 or |R| = 1 is 2−Ω(N). The cover may depend on the law and on n. The constants in its dimension bound and in the relative mass bound do not depend on the later selector or channel sizes.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.2
candidates.name: Status preparation
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.2 (Status preparation).
candidates.statement: Along a subsequence, the unit law can be prepared with final pin dimension at most K and the final per-leaf bounds of Lemma 4.5, at relative mass cost 2−o(N), so that one of the following descriptions applies. (i) There is no prediction as in Definition 9.1 on the first-peeled law. The effective spaces are still the first ones. For independent units, the mass admitting an admissible injecting small table is greater than .99. (ii) A prediction with fixed αi, c and common classes ei is retained. The old marks and exceptions are preserved, and Equation (9.1) has uniform o(1) error on every retained unit. The mass admitting an admissible injecting table satisfying Equation (9.3) is bounded below by a positive constant. (iii) Both prediction classes are zero, and every retained unit satisfies the exact identities pi = T(λi, ·) + a on all of X, i = 1, 2. There is a set of leaf pairs of mass at least c2N−4 under the final leaf mixture, for a fixed c2 > 0, with phase compatibility determined by the two leaves. For each such pair one can choose a specific injecting compatible table whose two separate orientation admissibility filters have masses at least a0 > 0. The constants c2, a0 are independent of n. In every case the mixed joint density is at most 2(D+o(1))N µ2, and its individual marginals are at most M2o(N)µ. Relative to the stored leaf bases and pin images, all numerical table formats, unary statuses, old-mark coordinates and exception-set descriptions have bounded length in n. The extra exact pins are used only in case (iii).

candidates.label: Theorem 11.1
candidates.name: Weak product comparison
candidates.heading: Theorem 11.1 (Weak product comparison).
candidates.statement: Let Wn be any sequence of real functions on Kn with ∥Wn∥∞ ≤ B, where B is fixed. Extend it to the product of the single-key spaces with the same bound. For every ε > 0 there are constants L, C < ∞, independent of n, and functions Sn(k1, . . . , kr) = L X a=1 ca,n r Y j=1 fa,j,n(kj), |ca,n| ≤ C, |fa,j,n| ≤ 1, (11.1) with the following properties. (i) For arbitrary global unary functions gj,n of bound one, | Z (Wn − Sn) Y j gj,n(kj) dνn| ≤ ε (11.2) for all sufficiently large n. (ii) Under any mixed unit law satisfying (10.8), outside an exponentially small exceptional set of orientations, sup |wj|≤1 |EzAn(O, z)(Wn − Sn)(K(O, z)) Y j wj(O, zj)| ≤ ε. (11.3) The unary input weights may depend on the entire fixed orientation and on any additional marks fixed with it. The exceptional set is independent of these weights. The functions fa,j,n are global key functions; they can be chosen to be indicators of sets, or finite linear combinations of such indicators with uniformly bounded complexity. They do not depend on the sampled orientation. The constants may depend on B, ε and the fixed template and construction parameters, but not on n. An additional orientation-only filter of bound one may multiply (11.3) without changing it. In particular, after averaging normalized leaves, the same error control applies to unnormalized admissibility-filtered query measures, even when the filter is chosen using the opposite leaf. No assertion is made for an arbitrary additional joint input filter.

candidates.label: Corollary 11.4
candidates.name: Factorized integration of the approximant
candidates.heading: Corollary 11.4 (Factorized integration of the approximant).
candidates.statement: For the structured sum in (11.1) and arbitrary bounded unary input weights, outside exponentially small mixed mass, EzAn(O, z)Sn(K(O, z)) Y j wj(O, zj) = κ L X a=1 ca,n Y j Ezj  fa,j,n(Kj(O, zj))wj(O, zj)  + o(1). (11.11) The error is uniform over the unary weights. An orientation-only filter may be included before averaging this identity over leaves.

candidates.label: Proposition 12.7
candidates.name: The limiting overlap obstruction
candidates.heading: Proposition 12.7 (The limiting overlap obstruction).
candidates.statement: Assume (12.3). In the common experiment of Lemma 12.4, almost every sampled pair of orientation records has the following property: there is no usable numerical option whose two orientation flags pass and for which, at every matched position, Z Ξl,q hθA tA,υA (ξ)hθB tB,υB (ξ) dml,q(ξ) > 0. (12.8)

candidates.label: Proposition 13.7
candidates.name: Positive-mass overlap
candidates.heading: Proposition 13.7 (Positive-mass overlap).
candidates.statement: For every positive-mass alternative of Proposition 9.2, some fixed numerical option has expected unnormalized successful-query overlap bounded below by a positive constant along a subsequence. Consequently it satisfies (7.3). This conclusion includes the prepared restrictions of reciprocal mass 2o(N) permitted there.

candidates.label: Proposition 14.4

manuscripts.title: A counterexample to the Colin de Verdière chromatic conjecture

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: There are finite graphs G of arbitrarily large order for which α(G) ≤ 2, µ(G) + 1 < |V (G)| 2 ≤ χ(G). In particular, the Colin de Verdière chromatic conjecture is false.

candidates.label: Theorem 1.2
candidates.name: Base graphs
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.2 (Base graphs).
candidates.statement: There is a constant a > 0 such that, for every β > 0, there are arbitrarily large integers m and graphs H on m vertices with α(H) ≤ 2 and the following properties. (G1) Every matching of size at least m/20, partitioned into classes of size at most am, contains two conflicting edges in different classes. (G2) Every matching of size at least βm and every vertex set of size at least βm contain an edge and a vertex in conflict. (G3) Every two vertex sets of size at least βm contain a cross hole. The two vertex sets in G3 may overlap.
candidates.boundary: manual: ends at “The two vertex sets in G3 may overlap.”

candidates.label: Corollary 1.3
candidates.name: Fractional-colouring obstruction
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.3 (Fractional-colouring obstruction).
candidates.statement: There are finite nonempty simple graphs G of arbitrarily large order for which χf (G) ≥ |V (G)| α(G) ≥ |V (G)| 2 > κ(G) + 1 ≥ µ(G) + 1 ≥ h(G).

candidates.label: Corollary 1.4
candidates.name: A linear list-colouring bound
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.4 (A linear list-colouring bound).
candidates.statement: Let C be the absolute integer in OpenAI [24, Theorem 1.1]. Every finite nonempty simple graph G satisfies χlist(G) ≤ C µ(G) + 1  .

candidates.label: Proposition 2.4
candidates.name: Finite tree principle
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.4 (Finite tree principle).
candidates.statement: For each index s, let P1,s, . . . , Pk,s be positive subspaces in a Lorentz space, whose dimension may depend on s. Fix a set D of pairs of distinct labels, and assume sup s dH(FPi,s , FPj,s ) ≤ D < ∞ ({i, j} ∈ D). After passing to a subsequence, there are a finite combinatorial tree T and a nonempty connected vertex set Si ⊆ V (T) for every label, with the following properties. (i) Si ∩ Sj ̸= ∅ for every {i, j} ∈ D. (ii) For every vertex x, called a bag, choose any Lorentz-orthonormal basis in every Pi,s with x ∈ Si. The Gram matrix of the concatenated list has operator norm bounded uniformly in s. The bound depends only on k, D, and not on the dimensions or on the bases. In particular, mutually orthogonal blocks can always be required to have intersecting subtrees.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.8
candidates.name: A common bag
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.8 (A common bag).
candidates.statement: Suppose the hypotheses of Theorems 2.6 and 2.7 hold in the same tree. Suppose additionally that Se ∩ Sv ̸= ∅ whenever the edge e and the vertex v ∈ V0 conflict. If q ≤ cm/4, there is a vertex x such that |{v ∈ V0 : x / ∈ Sv}| < 5q, X e: x∈Se we ≥ cm 2 . (2.14) If all edges of E have both endpoints in V0 and q ≤ cm/30, deleting every edge incident with a missing vertex leaves bag weight at least cm/3.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.1
candidates.name: Matrix obstruction
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.1 (Matrix obstruction).
candidates.statement: For every a ∈ (0, 1] there are constants β0(a) > 0 and m0(a) ∈ N with the following property. Let 0 < β ≤ β0(a), let m ≥ m0(a), and let G be an m-vertex graph satisfying the following conditions: (i) Every matching of size at least m/20, partitioned into classes of size at most am, contains two conflicting edges in different classes. (ii) Every matching of size at least βm and every vertex set of size at least βm contain a conflicting edge–point pair. (iii) Every two vertex sets of size at least βm have a cross hole. Then there is s0 = s0(G, a, β) such that, for every integer s ≥ s0, every real symmetric well-signed matrix M for the clique blow-up G[Ks] with exactly one negative eigenvalue satisfies rank M > ms 2 + 1. Consequently µ(G[Ks]) + 1 < ms/2 for all these s.

candidates.label: Theorem 5.4
candidates.name: Distribution tests
candidates.heading: Theorem 5.4 (Distribution tests).
candidates.statement: There is a constant ηcol > 0, depending only on the early parameters and M, with the following property. Fix any L < ∞ after ηcol and before the selector and channel parameters; choose all remaining parameters in the order of Equation (4.4) and Section A. For every sufficiently large n, the law π constructed above satisfies both conclusions. 34 (i) Let (A, c) have a probability law on units marked by a colour in any fixed finite palette. The colour may be randomized conditional on A. Write σ1, σ2 for the endpoint marginals of its projected unit law σ, and suppose σ1 ≤ Mπ, σ2 ≤ Mπ, σ ≤ 23000gN π2 , Pr(c = j) ≤ ηcol for every j. (5.8) For two independent draws (A, c), (B, c′), Pr(A ▷◁ B, c ̸= c′ ) ≥ 2−100gN . (ii) Let A have a unit law σ and let z be an independent point with law θ, where σ1 ≤ Lπ, σ2 ≤ Lπ, σ ≤ 23000gN π2 , θ ≤ Lπ. (5.9) Then Pr(A ▷◁ z) ≥ 2−100gN . The threshold for n may depend on the fixed palette and on L. All inequalities between measures are pointwise on their finite spaces.

candidates.label: Corollary 5.7
candidates.name: Colours and actual leaf weights
candidates.heading: Corollary 5.7 (Colours and actual leaf weights).
candidates.statement: For a law satisfying Equation (5.8), discard colours whose mass is below 2−ζN , and apply Theorem 5.6(a) to each remaining conditional colour law. The total discarded mass tends to zero exponentially, the leaves have at most K1 pins and satisfy Equation (5.10), and each leaf has an absolute density bound 2(D+K1+1)N P0 2 . With their actual retained masses these leaves form a mixed law whose endpoint marginals are bounded by (1 + o(1))Mπ. Any subsequent combined restriction of mass 2−o(N) has the first-pin freshness in Equation (5.11), after the trimming in Theorem 5.6(b).

candidates.label: Corollary 5.8
candidates.name: An independent pair as an unpinned leaf
candidates.heading: Corollary 5.8 (An independent pair as an unpinned leaf).
candidates.statement: Let θ ≤ Lπ, and draw two independent θ-points. The probability that they form an internal hole is 2−Ω(N). Their law conditioned on being a unit is a single leaf with no pins, with endpoint marginals at most (1 + o(1))Lπ, and it satisfies Equation (5.10) for every rank t ≥ 1. Its effective spaces C1, C2, defined in Section 6, are consequently zero.

candidates.label: Theorem 7.3
candidates.name: Gradient realization
candidates.heading: Theorem 7.3 (Gradient realization).
candidates.statement: Suppose two units in fixed leaves have lists satisfying (7.2), the binary prescriptions yielding (7.3), equal matched keys, and an admissible injecting small table. Freeze their actual cross Gram entries whenever either argument is a pin or a key direction. Then there are abstract cross bilinear forms on the full nominal spaces, extending all these frozen entries, whose primal-versus-channel entries satisfy uzUi = r(viz) on X (i and z in opposite units). (7.4) Only the primal-versus-channel entries need be prescribed in the final test. Their number is at most 16|E|h dim B = O(n), with its coefficient fixed before M0. Agreement of the actual cross Grams with these entries produces all four cross holes, with witnesses (viz, vzi).

candidates.label: Proposition 8.1
candidates.name: Filtered collision criterion
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.1 (Filtered collision criterion).
candidates.statement: Let σA, σB be two laws on units, possibly carrying finitely many colour or type marks. After forgetting these marks, suppose each law has density at most 23000gN relative to π ⊗ π. For O ∈ {A, B}, let e σO be a normalized restriction of σO of relative mass at least 2−o(N), decomposed into leaves satisfying (5.11). On each side mix the leaves with their actual masses in e σO. Fix a required predicate Ψ(A, B) on the marked units and an allowed leaf-pair indicator Jn. Use only numerical query options whose joint acceptance on an allowed leaf pair, including their separate orientation filters, implies Ψ(A, B). Suppose these accepted queries satisfy Eindependent leaf pairJn(ℓA, ℓB) Z dAdB dνn ≥ 2−o(N) . (8.3) Then independent draws A ∼ σA, B ∼ σB satisfy Ψ(A, B) and have all four cross holes with probability at least 2−(kmax+.03)N−o(N) . (8.4) It suffices to obtain (8.3) after skipping some leaf pairs, or after summing over a bounded number of numerical options. In particular, a positive subsequential overlap lower bound yields (8.4) along that subsequence. With σA = σB and Ψ the distinct-colour test, the conclusion retains that test. The statement also applies when the two sides have different prescribed law types.

candidates.label: Theorem 9.3
candidates.name: Phase alternative
candidates.heading: Theorem 9.3 (Phase alternative).
candidates.statement: Suppose a marked-unit law σ satisfies σi ≤ Λπ (i = 1, 2), σ ≤ 2(D+.01)N P0 2 , where Λ is fixed before the channel size, and suppose ∆O ̸= 0 throughout. For all sufficiently large n, one can retain a sublaw of relative mass at least δph > 0, depending only on the early parameters, such that one of the following holds for independent draws A, B: (i) every nontrivial phase mean E(−1)uB,S(∆A)+uA,R(∆B) , (S, R) ̸= (∅, ∅), has absolute value less than .005; (ii) writing F(A, B) = uB,{1,2}(∆A), one has F(A, B) = 0 for every pair of retained units, and every displayed mean for which |S| = 1 or |R| = 1 is 2−Ω(N). All marks remain in their first effective spaces. No additional image directions are pinned. Neither the retained-mass bound nor the tiny-cover dimension used in the proof depends on selector or channel sizes; the lower bound required of h may depend on Λ.

candidates.label: Corollary 9.4
candidates.name: A uniform phase compatibility margin
candidates.heading: Corollary 9.4 (A uniform phase compatibility margin).
candidates.statement: On either retained law of Theorem 9.3, for each fixed c ∈ F2 and all sufficiently large n, P{uB,1(∆A) = uB,2(∆A) = uA,1(∆B) = uA,2(∆B) = c} ≥ 1/32. (9.18) Also P{F(A, B) + F(B, A) = 0} ≥ .49, and each single prescribed phase bit has probability at least .49.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.5
candidates.name: Status preparation
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.5 (Status preparation).
candidates.statement: There are constants δ∗, c∗ > 0, fixed before the selector and channel sizes, with the following property. Along a subsequence, the original pooled unit law has a restriction of mass at least δ∗ whose first pin dimension is at most K1 and whose normalized leaves satisfy Equation (5.11). One of the following descriptions applies. (i) There is no prediction as in Theorem 10.1 on the first pooled law before the final negligible leaf trimming. For independent draws from the prepared law, the probability of an admissible injecting actual small table is greater than .99. 71 (ii) A prediction with fixed αi, c and common classes ei is retained. Its marks and exceptions are preserved, and Equation (10.1) has uniform o(1) error on every retained unit. If both classes vanish, Equation (10.3) is exact on every unit. For independent draws from the prepared law, the probability of an admissible injecting actual table satisfying Equation (10.8) is at least 1/64. In particular the corresponding successful pair event, measured in two draws from the original pooled law, has mass at least c∗. One may take δ∗ = 10−6δph 64 , c∗ = δ2 ∗ 64 , 0 < ηcol < c∗ 4 , (10.9) where 0 < δph ≤ 1 is the early retained-mass constant in Theorem 9.3. The colour bound in Equation (10.9) can be chosen using the initial M and early geometric constants only; the marginal constant L of the second distribution test does not enter it. After forgetting colour and other marks, the prepared law σ′ satisfies σ′ i ≤ M δ∗ π (i = 1, 2), σ′ ≤ 2(D+o(1))N P0 2 . (10.10) The endpoint primal marginals consequently have the same constant bound relative to pr∗ P0. Every normalized leaf has joint density at most 2O(N)P0 2 . The successful table event is detected by a finite list of numerical tables and separate unary orientation flags, together with leaf-pair tests. The size of this list is fixed in n, but need not be early.

candidates.label: Corollary 10.6
candidates.name: Removing equal colours
candidates.heading: Corollary 10.6 (Removing equal colours).
candidates.statement: Suppose the original colour masses are pγ ≤ ηcol. The successful prepared pair event of Theorem 10.5, with the further requirement that its two colours differ, has mass at least c∗ − ηcol > 3c∗/4 in the original pooled law.

candidates.label: Theorem 12.1
candidates.name: Weak product comparison
candidates.heading: Theorem 12.1 (Weak product comparison).
candidates.statement: Let Wn be any sequence of real functions on Kn with ∥Wn∥∞ ≤ B, where B is fixed. Extend it to the product of the single-key spaces with the same 87 bound. For every ε > 0 there are constants L, C < ∞, independent of n, and functions Sn(k1, . . . , kr) = L X a=1 ca,n r Y j=1 fa,j,n(kj), |ca,n| ≤ C, |fa,j,n| ≤ 1, (12.1) with the following properties. (i) For arbitrary global unary functions gj,n of bound one, | Z (Wn − Sn) Y j gj,n(kj) dνn| ≤ ε (12.2) for all sufficiently large n. (ii) Under any mixed unit law satisfying (11.8), outside an exponentially small exceptional set of orientations, sup |wj|≤1 |EzAn(O, z)(Wn − Sn)(K(O, z)) Y j wj(O, zj)| ≤ ε. (12.3) The unary input weights may depend on the entire fixed orientation and on any additional marks fixed with it. The exceptional set is independent of these weights. Thus one may prescribe channel flags such as pi in a unary weight without making them common key tests or asserting positivity for their individual values. The functions fa,j,n are global key functions; they can be chosen to be indicators of sets, or finite linear combinations of such indicators with uniformly bounded complexity. They do not depend on the sampled orientation. The constants may depend on B, ε and the fixed template and construction parameters, but not on n. An additional orientation-only filter of bound one may multiply (12.3) without changing it. In particular, after averaging normalized leaves, the same error control applies to unnormalized admissibility-filtered query measures, even when the filter is chosen using the opposite leaf. No assertion is made for an arbitrary additional joint input filter. For distinct marked laws, use their fixed-weight mixture, with caps checked after forgetting the marks. A retained ordered type pair or different-colour condition is an orientation/leaf-pair filter, so the same conclusion applies before normalization. All leaf averages use their actual weights; no marginal hypothesis on a separately normalized colour class is needed.

candidates.label: Corollary 12.4
candidates.name: Factorized integration of the approximant
candidates.heading: Corollary 12.4 (Factorized integration of the approximant).
candidates.statement: For the structured sum in (12.1) and arbitrary bounded unary input weights, outside exponentially small mixed mass, EzAn(O, z)Sn(K(O, z)) Y j wj(O, zj) = κ L X a=1 ca,n Y j Ezj  fa,j,n(Kj(O, zj))wj(O, zj)  + o(1). (12.11) The error is uniform over the unary weights. An orientation-only filter may be included before averaging this identity over leaves. In particular the same statement applies to marked mixtures and retained type/colour pairs as in Theorem 12.1.

candidates.label: Proposition 13.7
candidates.name: The limiting overlap obstruction
candidates.heading: Proposition 13.7 (The limiting overlap obstruction).
candidates.statement: Assume (13.3). In the common experiment of Theorem 13.4, almost every sampled pair of orientation records with J(Z) = 1 has the following property: there is no usable numerical option whose two orientation flags pass and for which, at every matched position, Z Ξl,q hθA tA,υA (ξ)hθB tB,υB (ξ) dml,q(ξ) > 0. (13.8)

candidates.name: Positive-mass overlap
candidates.heading: Proposition 14.7 (Positive-mass overlap).
candidates.statement: Consider two independent unit laws with actual leaf weights, the mixed caps (11.8), the final per-leaf image bounds, and a permitted-pair indicator Jn as in Section 13. Suppose their common model has positive mass of pairs with J = 1 admitting a passed injecting table whose scalar system is soluble after every bounded exclusion used by Theorem 14.6. Then some fixed numerical option has expected unnormalized, permitted-pair overlap 106 bounded below by a positive constant along a subsequence. Consequently it satisfies (8.3), with the same permitted-pair predicate. The two laws need not coincide. If the original laws additionally satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 8.1, its probability bound holds along the same subsequence, with any initial restrictions of reciprocal mass 2o(N) charged to that probability.

candidates.label: Proposition 14.8
candidates.name: Different-colour conflicts
candidates.heading: Proposition 14.8 (Different-colour conflicts).
candidates.statement: Let the early constant ηcol > 0 satisfy ηcol < 1 4 c∗, c∗ := δ2 ∗ 64 , where δ∗ is the retained-mass margin in (10.9). This choice depends on the original endpoint bound M and the early geometric constants, and precedes the selector and channel dimensions. For every fixed finite palette and all sufficiently large n, a unit law with both endpoint marginals bounded by Mπ, pair law after forgetting colour bounded by 23000gN π2, and each colour of mass at most ηcol satisfies Pr{A and B have four cross holes and different colours} ≥ 2−100gN , 107 where A, B are independent draws from that law. manuscripts.title: A linear list-coloring bound in terms of the Hadwiger number

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: There is an absolute integer C ≥ 1 such that every finite nonempty simple graph G satisfies ℓ(G) ≤ Ch(G).

candidates.label: Corollary 1.2
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.2.
candidates.statement: Every finite nonempty simple graph G satisfies χ(G) ≤ Ch(G), with the constant C in Theorem 1.1.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.1
candidates.name: Fractional minor bound
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.1 (Fractional minor bound).
candidates.statement: Every graph P satisfies f(P) ≤ 4h(P).
candidates.cited_by: This follows from the stronger bound f(P) ≤ 2h(P) of Reed and Seymour [23, Statement (1.3)].
references: [23] Bruce Reed and Paul Seymour. Fractional colouring and Hadwiger’s conjecture. Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B, 74:147–152, 1998. URL https://cgm.cs.mcgill.ca/~breed /SummerNSERC04/frachad.pdf.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.2
candidates.name: Ordinary-chromatic connectivity extraction
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.2 (Ordinary-chromatic connectivity extraction).
candidates.statement: If k ≥ 1 is an integer and χ(P) ≥ 7k, then P has a k-connected subgraph J with χ(J) ≥ χ(P) − 6k.
candidates.cited_by: We use the form stated in [5, Theorem 5.1], attributed there to Girão and Narayanan.
references: [5] Michelle Delcourt and Luke Postle. Reducing linear Hadwiger’s conjecture to coloring small graphs. Journal of the American Mathematical Society, 38(2):481–507, 2025. doi: 10.109 0/jams/1047. URL https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.01633v5. Theorem locators refer to arXiv:2108.01633v5, March 5, 2024.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.3
candidates.name: Grouping terminals
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.3 (Grouping terminals).
candidates.statement: There is an absolute integer γ ≥ 1 such that the following holds. In a γm-connected graph, every partition of m ≥ 1 distinct terminals into nonempty groups can be realized by pairwise disjoint connected vertex sets, one containing each group.
candidates.cited_by: This is a consequence of the highly linked graph theorem of Bollobás and Thomason [3]; we use the case with second knitting parameter one in [5, Definition 5.7 and Theorem 5.8].
references: [3] Béla Bollobás and Andrew Thomason. Highly linked graphs. Combinatorica, 16(3):313–320, 1996. doi: 10.1007/BF01261316. URL https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01261316.

[5] Michelle Delcourt and Luke Postle. Reducing linear Hadwiger’s conjecture to coloring small graphs. Journal of the American Mathematical Society, 38(2):481–507, 2025. doi: 10.109 0/jams/1047. URL https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.01633v5. Theorem locators refer to arXiv:2108.01633v5, March 5, 2024.

manuscripts.title: The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: The Euclidean plane has no proper five-coloring, even when arbitrary color classes are al- lowed. Consequently, 6 ≤ χ(R2 ) ≤ 7.

candidates.label: Theorem 1.3
candidates.name: Transfer of colorability
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.3 (Transfer of colorability).
candidates.statement: For every positive integer k, in ZFC, a proper k-coloring of R2 exists ⇐⇒ a weak measurable k-coloring of R2 exists. (1.1)

candidates.label: Theorem 1.4
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.4.
candidates.statement: There is no weak measurable five-coloring of the Euclidean plane.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.5
candidates.name: Positive five-color badness
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.5 (Positive five-color badness).
candidates.statement: There is a constant δ > 0 with the following properties. (i) For every coloring c : R2 → {1, . . . , 5} and every normalized finitely additive left-invariant measure µ on all subsets of the plane-isometry group E(2), the invariant-mean badness satisfies p µ 5 (c) := µ {T ∈ E(2) : c(T−1 0) = c(T−1 1)}  ≥ δ, where R2 is identified with C. (ii) If c is a Lebesgue-measurable five-coloring with two linearly independent periods, then P(c(A) = c(A + U)) ≥ δ, where A is uniform in a fundamental parallelogram and U is an independent uniform unit direction. For any Lebesgue-measurable five-coloring, if the conditional square-table frequencies P c(AR) = c(AR + U) | AR + U ∈ [−R, R]2  (R > 1) converge as R → ∞, their limit is at least δ; here AR is uniform in [−R, R]2 and independent of U.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.3
candidates.name: Rigidity of wild character laws
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.3 (Rigidity of wild character laws).
candidates.statement: Every K-invariant probability measure ν on D with ν(C) = 0 is Haar measure. Equivalently, writing mD for normalized Haar measure, ν is wild =⇒ ν = mD. (2.2)

candidates.label: Proposition 4.2
candidates.name: From proper to weak measurable colorings
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.2 (From proper to weak measurable colorings).
candidates.statement: Let k be a positive integer. If the plane admits an unrestricted proper k-coloring, then it admits a weak measurable k-coloring.

candidates.label: Corollary 5.4
candidates.name: Sixty-degree exclusion
candidates.heading: Corollary 5.4 (Sixty-degree exclusion).
candidates.statement: At every fixed center x, Px(f ) ∩ Px(R f ) = ∅ for almost every f ∈ S. (5.7)

candidates.label: Proposition 5.6

candidates.heading: Proposition 5.6 (Palette cardinality).
candidates.statement: For every center x ∈ R2, 1 ≤ |Px(e)| ≤ 2 for almost every e ∈ S. (5.12) The angular exceptional set may depend on x.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.5
candidates.name: Local finiteness of cyclic centers
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.5 (Local finiteness of cyclic centers).
candidates.statement: The set L = {x ∈ R2 : Γx contains a cycle} (6.4) is closed and locally finite: it has finite intersection with every compact subset of the plane.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.1
candidates.name: A cycle of common exclusion continua
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.1 (A cycle of common exclusion continua).
candidates.statement: For the weak measurable five-coloring under consideration, there exist an integer ℓ ∈ {3, 4, 5}, distinct labels i0, . . . , iℓ−1 ∈ I, a point x ∈ R2, and a radius ρ > 0 with the following properties. For each edge ijij+1 of the simple label cycle, with indices modulo ℓ, there are a compact connected set Kj ⊂ B(x, ρ), a direction vj ∈ S, and a sequence qj,k ∈ Kj \ {x} such that 1. x ∈ Kj and Kj ∩ ∂B(x, ρ) ̸= ∅; 2. qj,k → x and (qj,k − x)/|qj,k − x| → vj; 42 3. both endpoint supports are excluded from the same open set: Hij ∩ ∆(Kj) = Hij+1 ∩ ∆(Kj) = ∅. The extracted cycle need not consist of edges of Γx.

manuscripts.title: Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: For each fixed integer k ≥ 3 there are constants Ck, ck, εk > 0 such that, for every N ≥ 2, rk(N) ≤ CkN exp −ck(log N)εk  . (1.1) Equivalently, there is Ak ≥ 1 such that an α-dense subset of [N] contains a nonconstant k-term progression whenever log N ≥ Ak 2 + log(1/α) Ak , 0 < α ≤ 1. (1.2)

candidates.label: Corollary 1.2
candidates.name: Divergent reciprocal sums
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.2 (Divergent reciprocal sums).
candidates.statement: Every set A ⊆ N with P a∈A a−1 = ∞ contains nonconstant arithmetic progressions of every finite length.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.1
candidates.name: Triangular increment
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.1 (Triangular increment).
candidates.statement: There are fixed D = Dk, η = ηk > 0, and polynomials with degrees depending only on k having the following property. Suppose p ≥ 2, a ≥ e−p, and a progression-free input on a positive-dimensional integer box has a certificate (2.2), with width logs Qh = log(2/wh). If every root side is sufficiently large with logarithmic cutoff polynomial in p, the dimension data, and all Qh, then either the hypotheses are impossible or a root slice carries a new certificate at threshold (1 + η)a. The new cell retains the determining data through exact integer reparametrizations and adds at most d0 = (2 + p)Ck fresh absolute slots together with downward preparation copies. Its dimensions d′ i and width logs Q′ i satisfy d′ i − di ≤ d0 + Pi(p, di+1, . . . , dD), (2.3) Q′ i − Qi ≤ P′ i (p, all dimension forecasts, Qi+1, . . . , QD). (2.4) The root slice cost has polynomial logarithmic bound in all the same data, now including every Qi. Polynomial exponents and the fixed gain are independent of the number of increments. Gap and discount choices can be made in advance from the dimension and cut-count forecasts.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.4
candidates.name: Pathwise detection and approximation
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.4 (Pathwise detection and approximation).
candidates.statement: Prescribe finitely many testing degrees in the fixed allowed range, local test complexities, slice costs, input caps, and accuracies. The later parameters of the one-layer construction can be chosen once so that the following assertions hold for this same ensemble, uniformly in the center and the site input. For cold-pre requests, if a cold-pre-bounded input satisfies Xr(g) ≥ a > 0, with log(1/a) bounded by cold-pre data, then g correlates in uniform parent measure with an ambient atom of cold-pre complexity, and the logarithm of the reciprocal correlation has a cold-pre bound. Every |g| ≤ 1 can also be approximated in Xr, to the prescribed cold-pre accuracy, by a linear combination of such atoms with cold-pre coefficient mass and number of terms. If r < j and the requests are warm, every warm-bounded input with Xr(g) ≥ a > 0 and a warm bound for log(1/a) correlates in µc with an ambient atom of warm complexity, with a warm bound for the logarithm of the reciprocal correlation. The atoms, coefficient mass, and number of terms in the Xr approximation also have warm bounds. These bounds may use the omission threshold but do not use Qj or the height of W. For a specified larger input cap, include its logarithm in the request budget and rescale. Increasing the requested accuracy, test, or path budgets changes the corresponding warm or cold-pre output logarithms polynomially. All path probabilities and testing suprema refer to the law before productive paths are selected.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.1
candidates.name: Prepared system with triangular costs
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.1 (Prepared system with triangular costs).
candidates.statement: Given a triangular two-box certificate, forecast dimension bounds and descending numerical budgets in the sense of Definition 2.3. After polynomially many rank-cut transactions, there is a certificate with an arbitrarily small prescribed total proportional target discount such that every rank-stop probability in the actual current sampling procedure is at most its prescribed bound. The procedure may restart its tests after every transaction. The dimensions added at block i are polynomial in the dimensions strictly above i. The increase in its width logarithm is polynomial in dimension data, p, and higher-level numerical budgets, and is independent of its own initial width logarithm except for carrying that logarithm additively. Root slice costs and sufficient root-side cutoffs have polynomial logarithms in the full eventual budgets.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.2
candidates.name: Forward mass
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.2 (Forward mass).
candidates.statement: For any sufficiently small fixed η > 0, a prepared certificate at threshold a gives a surviving set of terminal injective paths whose expected terminal input mean, with stopped paths counted as zero, is at least (1 − η)a. The input is pulled back successively and masked by no bad flag at every active layer. Its support is progression-free. At least a fraction ηa of terminal paths have mean at least (1 − 2η)a, after harmless adjustment of the loss constants. The rank-stop probability at layer h need only have inverse logarithmic cost polynomial in the data at layers ≥ h. Discards immediately after that layer can be requested warm-small after charging the feasible-center proportions of layers > h. Thus this proposition does not require a lower-layer width in a higher-layer rank budget.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.4
candidates.name: Scalar comparison
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.4 (Scalar comparison).
candidates.statement: Suppose a set of productive modular-good paths has probability at least τ, with log(1/τ) pre bounded, and each has a specified pre-cost slice. Consider bounded scores depending on site and auxiliary labels. Assume that, after partitioning into pre-count many pre-cost slices, each score is uniformly approximable at the required pre accuracy, both on actual path arguments and on the joint support of K, by the same menu of bounded site functions. A bounded number of successive increases of these pre bounds is allowed. Then, outside a set of paths smaller than the productive probability, the actual scalar averages and their K integrals differ by an arbitrarily prescribed pre-small error. This holds simultaneously for a pre-count menu of scores and for path-dependent slice choices. At active layers it also holds after multiplying a score by the no-bad-flag indicator. It is valid either for normalized slice averages or with full-box mass retained, paying the explicit slice fractions. The budget is warm for passive uses and cold pre otherwise.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.8
candidates.name: Passive micro replacement
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.8 (Passive micro replacement).
candidates.statement: Suppose j > s and the ascent format holds on a warm-inverse fraction of paths at a fixed parent and feasible center. Use the group and the two fields of Lemma 7.5. There is a single ambient ordinary filtered polynomial gU (u) ∈ G0 of degree at most s, with no β argument, for which a warm-inverse fraction of the productive paths have warm-cost subslices on which replacing gψ by gU ◦ ψ preserves a positive signed full-mass score of warm size, after the allowed small target discounts. Both inherited cutoff functions and all their exact determining conditions are retained.

candidates.label: Corollary 7.9
candidates.name: Passive scalar return
candidates.heading: Corollary 7.9 (Passive scalar return).
candidates.statement: After Proposition 7.8, one can select a modular-good path and its retained warm-cost subslice for which the forecasting measure K of Lemma 7.3 has a signed surplus of warm size. After one further small proportional target discount, its parallel residue matching can be imposed modulo an integer M∗ with warm logarithmic cost. The site payoffs still evaluate the original cutoffs on gU (u), with the exact old determining conditions.

candidates.label: Theorem 8.2
candidates.name: Active replacement
candidates.heading: Theorem 8.2 (Active replacement).
candidates.statement: Fix the prepared parent and a feasible center at a layer j ≤ s. Assume the modified sampler, scalar comparison, and major-decomposition contracts established above. Let G0 be a controlled filtered group of degree r, with a strong rational projection π0 : G0 → Y . Suppose a pre-inverse fraction of the available paths are modular-good in the sense of Equation (6.3), and each such path has a polynomial gψ(v, z) whose logarithmic coordinates have bounded total degree, adapted in v at each fixed z, and satisfy the formal identity π0 gψ(v, z) = PY (Xψ(v, z); z), Xψ = (ψ, β ◦ ψ). (8.1) Here PY (X; z) is fixed on those paths, weighted filtered in X, and polynomial in z, with bounded total degree. There is no bound on the coefficients of either polynomial. Let the two external fields satisfy Definition 8.1. Suppose their signed score, with the original slice mask 1S and full parameter mass, is at least δ > 0: Et1S(t) h 1no bad(t)F− ψ,ψ(t)(θ, e t)(gψ(t)Γ0 ) − λF+ ψ,ψ(t)(θ, e t)(gψ(t)Γ0 ) i ≥ δ, (8.2) 61 where 0 < λ ≤ 1. Include the original slice cost, the short-label range bounds, and log(1/δ) in the prescribed preliminary data. All path probabilities refer to the original ensemble, with discarded paths retained as zero mass; subsequent selections are subsets of the modular-good productive paths just specified. For any prescribed 0 < η < δ/2, include log(1/η) in that request. Then one retained modular-good path admits a stochastic polynomial g♯ (X, θ, e t) ∈ G0 , π0 g♯ (X, θ, e t) = PY (X; z) (8.3) whose K-score, with the same slice and flag masks and the expectation of the two payoffs, is at least δ − η. A stochastic polynomial means a polynomial formula with random constant parameters, sampled independently of its arguments. Its total logarithmic-coordinate degree is bounded in terms of the input degree bounds only; its coefficients need not be bounded. A filtered-degree bound in the original parameters is not asserted. On the joint chart and exact-inactive locus zI(X) = zI(tI), (8.4) each expected payoff separately is independent of the representatives chosen for the parallel residue labels, with all other data fixed. This is a pointwise statement for every admissible label choice. The retained path fraction and all auxiliary logarithmic costs may have cold pre-cost. The number of successive polynomial budget increases and all degree increases depend only on the fixed input degrees. Thus, when δ, the original slice, and η have warm bounds, the resulting score and slice still have those bounds.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.1
candidates.name: One-layer extraction
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.1 (One-layer extraction).
candidates.statement: Under these hypotheses, after a prescribed small propor- tional discount of the target, one obtains a parent slice and a pair of cutoff boxes which add the current raw block bj to the determining system. The inherited determining polynomials and integer arguments are restored exactly. The new slice and current-block congruence have warm log cost, and the current radius r′ j satisfies log wj r′ j ≤ poly(warm log data). The logarithm of the reciprocal returned full-mass score has cold cost at layer j. At passive layers the absolute weights are unchanged. At active layers a fixed multiplicative increase of those weights suffices; determining weights remain exactly their original weights. All degree bounds are independent of the budget dimensions.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.2
candidates.name: Triangular dimension bounds
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.2 (Triangular dimension bounds).
candidates.statement: For one round, the increase in the dimension of weight i is bounded by d0 plus a fixed polynomial in the incoming dimensions strictly above i. The number of preparation cuts and all structural variable counts are polynomial in the incoming dimensions and p. For a proposed run of T = Ok(1 + p) rounds on an interval, starting without slots, all these quantities admit polynomial bounds in 2 + p, chosen before any numerical precision.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.3
candidates.name: Triangular width bounds
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.3 (Triangular width bounds).
candidates.statement: The choices above can be made with fixed polynomial logarithmic bounds. They give, in one round, Qout j ≤ qj + Pj(p, d∗, q>j). (10.2) where Pj is a fixed polynomial independent of qj and of all lower width logs. The total root logarithmic slice loss and the sufficient root log-side cutoff are polynomial in p, d∗ and all incoming width logs. For the interval run of Ok(1 + p) rounds in Proposition 10.2, starting without slots and with trivial width data, these width logs and the sums of root costs are polynomial in 2 + p.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.4
candidates.name: Finite-horizon closure
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.4 (Finite-horizon closure).
candidates.statement: There are constants Ck > 0 and Ak ≥ 1 such that a progression-free subset of [N] of density α > 0 cannot satisfy log N ≥ Ck 2 + log(1/α) Ak .

candidates.label: Proposition 11.1
candidates.name: Dyadic weighted summation
candidates.heading: Proposition 11.1 (Dyadic weighted summation).
candidates.statement: For w : N → [0, ∞), set Sk(w) = ∞ X m=0 rk(2m ) max 2m≤n<2m+1 w(n). If A ⊆ N contains no nonconstant k-term progression, then X a∈A w(a) ≤ Sk(w). Consequently, whenever Sk(w) < ∞, divergence of the weighted sum forces a nonconstant k-term progression.

candidates.label: Corollary 11.2
candidates.name: Uniform harmonic bound
candidates.heading: Corollary 11.2 (Uniform harmonic bound).
candidates.statement: There is Hk < ∞ such that every k-term-progression- free A ⊆ N satisfies X a∈A 1 a ≤ Hk. One may take Hk = P m≥0 2−mrk(2m).

candidates.label: Corollary 11.3
candidates.name: Stretched-exponential weights
candidates.heading: Corollary 11.3 (Stretched-exponential weights).
candidates.statement: Every k-term-progression-free set has a uniformly bounded sum for each of the weights wa(n) = exp(a(log n)ε) n , 0 < a < c, w∗,η(n) = exp(c(log n)ε) n log n (log log n)1+η , η > 0. The bound may depend on k and the displayed parameters. Divergence for either weight therefore forces a nonconstant k-term progression.

candidates.label: Corollary 11.4
candidates.name: Logarithmic weights and every length
candidates.heading: Corollary 11.4 (Logarithmic weights and every length).
candidates.statement: For every fixed B ≥ 0, if A ⊆ N satisfies X a∈A (log(2 + a))B a = ∞, then A contains nonconstant arithmetic progressions of every finite length.

candidates.label: Corollary 11.5
candidates.name: Harmonic tails
candidates.heading: Corollary 11.5 (Harmonic tails).
candidates.statement: There is C′ k > 0 such that every k-term-progression-free set A ⊆ N satisfies, for all sufficiently large real x, X a∈A a>x 1 a ≤ C′ k(log x)1−εk e−ck(log x)εk . In particular, for every 0 < a < ck, this tail is at most Ck,ae−a(log x)εk .

candidates.label: Theorem A.7
candidates.name: Quasipolynomial inverse theorem
candidates.heading: Theorem A.7 (Quasipolynomial inverse theorem).
candidates.statement: Fix an integer s ≥ 1. Let p ≥ 2. A unit- bounded function on an interval whose Us+1 norm is at least e−p correlates by at least B(p)−1 with a unit-bounded degree-s niltest of complexity P(p). The same conclusion holds on integer boxes and on products of cyclic groups, with the following dimension convention: for every fixed A ≥ 1, dimension n ≤ (2 + p)A is permitted, and the constants and polynomial exponents may depend only on s, A. On a product of cyclic groups the niltest is evaluated in the coordinatewise integer representatives.
candidates.cited_by: The interval assertion is the inverse theorem of Leng, Sah and Sawhney [35, Theorem 1.2]; for s = 1 it follows from Fourier inversion and Parseval.
references: [35] J. Leng, A. Sah, and M. Sawhney, Quasipolynomial bounds on the inverse theorem for the Gowers Us+1[N]-norm, arXiv:2402.17994v3, 2024.

candidates.label: Theorem C.1
candidates.name: Shift comparison
candidates.heading: Theorem C.1 (Shift comparison).
candidates.statement: For fixed d ≥ 1 and 0 < ϵ < 1, there is a constant C = C(d, ϵ) such that the following holds. Suppose that p ≥ 2, N ≥ exp((2 + p)C) is odd, and 0 ≤ f, g, J ≤ ep. Set P = (2 + p)C. If En(f − g)(n)T(n) ≤ e−P (T ∈ Td(P)), (C.1) then there is a set E ⊆ G, depending on f, g, J, with |E| ≤ e−pN, such that En f − (1 + ϵ)g  (n)J(n + h)T′ (n) ≤ e−p (h / ∈ E, T′ ∈ Td−1(p)). (C.2) The exceptional set is chosen before T′.

candidates.label: Proposition C.6
candidates.name: Degree-one shift comparison
candidates.heading: Proposition C.6 (Degree-one shift comparison).

candidates.label: Proposition C.12
candidates.name: Higher-degree propagation
candidates.heading: Proposition C.12 (Higher-degree propagation).
candidates.statement: Lemmas A.3, A.6, A.8, A.9, and B.1, together with the quasipolynomial inverse theorem, imply the propagation principle in Theorem C.1 for every fixed degree.

candidates.label: Proposition D.2
candidates.name: Positive counting
candidates.heading: Proposition D.2 (Positive counting).
candidates.statement: Let k ≥ 3, s = k − 2, and p ≥ 2. Given τ > 0, there exist ξ0 > 0 and C, depending only on k, τ, such that the following holds. Let H = Z/NZ with gcd(N, (k − 1)!) = 1, and fix 0 < ξ ≤ ξ0. Suppose 0 ≤ µi ≤ ep on H for 1 ≤ i ≤ k, |Eµi − 1| ≤ 2ξ, E µi − (1 + ξ)  T ≤ e−(2+p)C , 116 for all [0, 1]-valued niltests of degree at most s and complexity at most (2+p)C. If N ≥ exp((2+p)C), then, simultaneously for every subset I ⊆ [k], Ex,d Y i∈I µi(x + id) − 1 ≤ τ. (D.2)

candidates.label: Proposition D.3
candidates.name: Absolute increment on a fixed-dimensional box
candidates.heading: Proposition D.3 (Absolute increment on a fixed-dimensional box).
candidates.statement: Assume Theorem C.1. Fix k ≥ 3 and n ≥ 1. There are ξ > 0 and C, depending only on k, n, with the following property. Let Q = Qn j=1{0, . . . , Pj − 1}, where the Pj are distinct primes, and put p = max(2, log(1/α)). Suppose that min Pj ≥ exp((2 + p)C) and that f : Q → [0, 1] has mean α > 0 and support containing no nonconstant integer k-term progression. In the cyclic variable supplied by the Chinese remainder theorem there is a [0, 1]-valued niltest T of degree k − 2 and complexity at most (2 + p)C such that EQ f − (1 + ξ)α  T ≥ exp(−(2 + p)C ). (D.6)

candidates.label: Proposition D.7
candidates.name: Relative lifting
candidates.heading: Proposition D.7 (Relative lifting).
candidates.statement: Fix s ≥ 1, put k = s + 2, and fix a sufficiently large dimension n0 = n0(s) and ε0 > 0. There is an exponent E, depending only on these fixed parameters, with the following property. Fix the side-comparability constant R = 2n0+1. Let p ≥ 2, e−p ≤ a ≤ Λ ≤ 1, and suppose an absolute rule holds on every sufficiently large prime-sided box of dimension n0, with distinct sides and largest side at most R times the smallest: every progression-free input of mean at least a has, on a parameter slice of cost at most p, a degree-s patch of rank at most d0, complexity at most p, and score at least e−p against input minus Λ. The cutoff on every prime side is at most ep. Let Q be any box of dimension between 1 and p, with all sides at least exp((2 + p)E). Suppose 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 is progression-free on Q, and an old degree-s patch B of rank d and complexity at most p satisfies EQ(f − a)B ≥ e−p . Then some parameter slice of Q, of cost at most (2 + p)E, carries a degree-s patch B′ satisfying rank B′ ≤ d + d0, complexity(B′ ) ≤ (2 + p)E , E f − (1 − ε0)Λ  B′ ≥ exp(−(2 + p)E ). 122 There is also a separate impossibility alternative: if e−p ≤ a ≤ 1 and the absolute rule states that no such input of mean at least a exists, the old positive score is impossible. This alternative has no target parameter Λ. The exponent is independent of the absolute rule, of d, d0, and of every variable dimension included in p.

candidates.label: Proposition E.1
candidates.name: Scalar transfer
candidates.heading: Proposition E.1 (Scalar transfer).
candidates.statement: Fix the degree, an integer ℓ ≥ 2, and ε > 0. There are constants C, C′ > 0 with the following property; C′ depends only on ℓ, and one may take C′ = ℓ + 1. Let p ≥ 2, let I be an integer box of dimension n ≤ p and side lengths Hi, and let g : I → [0, 1] be a niltest of complexity at most p. Let 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 and e−p ≤ λ ≤ 2. Suppose, for every parameter slice B ⊆ I of log cost at most P = (2 + p)C, that EBfg ≤ λEBg + e−P . (E.1) Extend fg and g by zero. Choose integer x, V uniformly from product boxes at scales Hi and Hi/L, respectively, with V having ℓ columns. Sample t uniformly from an integer box in [−epL, epL]ℓ, possibly restricted to one residue in each coordinate modulo a common D ≤ ep, with every restricted side at least Le−2p. If L ≥ B(p) and mini Hi ≥ B(p)LC′ , then Pr x,V   Et fg − (1 + ε)λg  (x + V t) > e−p ≤ e−p . (E.2) The same conclusion holds when the outer law of (x, V ) is dominated by these product laws by ep, and for scale changes by eO(p), after polynomial changes of the log budgets. All complexity and precision requirements are prescribed before choosing L. The conditional law of t remains the stated uniform law on the prescribed parameter slice; arbitrary reweighting of t after observing (x, V ) is not included.

candidates.label: Proposition E.2
candidates.name: Stability of baseline marginals
candidates.heading: Proposition E.2 (Stability of baseline marginals).
candidates.statement: Let g be as in Proposition E.1. Select a finite collection of distinct primes l, with one power ql = lal per prime, where log ql and the logarithm of the number of primes have prescribed polynomial bounds. Regard u mod ql ∈ (Z/qlZ)n as a single coordinate. Prescribe δ > 0, an integer r0, and an initial set of mandatory coordinates, with log δ−1, r0, and the number of mandatory coordinates polynomially bounded. On any prescribed box of polynomial log cost, there is a decision tree whose nodes fix entire prime coordinates, with every leaf fixing all the prescribed mandatory coordinates, whose depth on every branch is polynomially bounded, and such that every nonempty leaf B satisfies |E[g | B, uJ = z] − E[g | B]| ≤ δ (|J| ≤ r0) (E.3) for every set J of still unfixed coordinates and every nonempty refinement uJ = z. The depth and the sufficient lower bound for the original side lengths have polynomial log bounds in the prescribed inputs, independently of the coefficients of the polynomial orbit defining g.

candidates.label: Proposition F.2
candidates.name: Constrained sampling
candidates.heading: Proposition F.2 (Constrained sampling).

A permitted site twist is a bounded Lipschitz function of u/H, (yh)h, multiplied by buffered chart cutoffs and by characters or residue indicators of (u, βh)h of a pre-bounded common modulus. manuscripts.title: A counterexample to Tachikawa's second conjecture

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Let k = F2(q, H1, H2), where q, H1, H2 are algebraically independent. There exist a finite-dimensional associative unital symmetric k-algebra A and a finite-dimensional unital left A-module M such that M is nonprojective and Exti A(M, M) = 0 for every integer i > 0. In particular, Tachikawa’s second conjecture is false.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.2
candidates.name: Homological conjectures
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.2 (Homological conjectures).
candidates.statement: Let A, M be as in Theorem 1.1. For every field extension K/k, put AK = K ⊗k A, MK = K ⊗k M, and ΓK = EndAK (AK ⊕ MK)op . Then ΓK is a finite-dimensional K-algebra with the following properties, in the category of finite left ΓK-modules. 1. Every term of the minimal injective resolution of ΓK is projective, but idΓK ΓK = ∞. 2. There is a nonzero simple module S such that Exti ΓK (S, ΓK) = 0 for every i ≥ 0. 3. There is a projective-injective Wakamatsu tilting module W which is not tilting. Consequently the classical, generalized, and strong Nakayama conjectures, the Auslander–Gorenstein conjecture, and the Wakamatsu tilting conjecture are false for finite-dimensional algebras over K.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.3
candidates.name: Finitistic dimensions
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.3 (Finitistic dimensions).
candidates.statement: Let k be the field in Theorem 1.1, let K/k be any field extension, and let ΓK be the algebra in Corollary 1.2. For every integer n ≥ 1, there is a finite- dimensional left ΓK-module Cn such that pdΓK Cn = n. Consequently ΓK has infinite little left finitistic dimension and infinite big left finitistic dimension.

candidates.label: Corollary 8.3
candidates.name: Idempotent stratifications
candidates.heading: Corollary 8.3 (Idempotent stratifications).
candidates.statement: For every field extension K/k and every integer L ≥ 1, there is an auxiliary finite-dimensional indecomposable symmetric K-algebra TL admitting an idempotent stratification of length at least L in the sense of Chen, Fang and Xi. In particular, TL has a nonzero proper stratifying ideal, and D(TL-Mod) admits a chain of at least L nontrivial standard recollements through successive corner algebras. Here Mod denotes all left modules and D is the unbounded derived category.
